newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Aug M3 boosted by sight, savings deposits.
newsitem.headline: German Aug M3 boosted by sight, savings deposits.

text.p: German M3 money supply grew a little more strongly in August and sight and savings deposits expanded strongly again in the period, the Bundesbank said on Thursday.
August M3 was boosted by buoyant lending and a decline in money capital formation, the Bundesbank added in a statement. Growth was also boosted by public borrowing.
An overhang from July also influenced August M3.
"Among the seasonally adjusted components of money supply, sight and savings deposits with a three month notice period expanded strongly again in August," the Bundesbank said.
August M3 rose by an annualised 8.7 percent, up from an 8.6 percent annualised rate in July.
The Bundesbank said public borrowing rose again in August versus July.
Bank lending to the public sector dropped by 0.7 billion marks. "But excluding seasonal effects, lending to the public sector strengthened again," the Bundesbank said.

"Monetary capital formation at the banks weakened in August. Overall the banks received in this month long term funds from domestic sources amounting to 7.2 billion marks, compared with 17.6 billion marks a year ago," it said.
Commenting on the slight rise in August M3 growth, the Bundesbank said: "A relatively high overhang from July was one contributing factor to this."
"In addition money supply expansion was boosted by more buoyant borrowing and a continued fall-off in money capital formation," the Bundesbank said.
"Cash in circulation, which had risen more strongly in July, on the other hand fell along with short term deposits," the statement said.
